harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired writer.py on node1. SIGHUP now reopens audit.log, releases the deleted descriptor, and continues under the same process. SIGTERM closes the log and exits with status 0. Existing A101/A100 records were preserved, and the fix survived the required node reboot.
actions_performed: Added deferred SIGHUP and SIGTERM handlers with guaranteed log closure.
Tested an actual deleted-open-file scenario before and after reboot.
Preserved root ownership, modes, SELinux enforcement, OS release, kernel, and archive data.
Removed test artifacts and confirmed no writer process or target descriptors remained.

evidence.requirement: SIGHUP reopens the current path, releases the old descriptor, and continues without restarting
evidence.summary: The same PID/start time moved from a deleted inode to the current audit.log inode, released all deleted descriptors, and continued adding records; repeated successfully after reboot.

evidence.requirement: SIGTERM closes the log and exits cleanly
evidence.summary: Both pre- and post-reboot tests exited with status 0, produced no writes after termination, and left no target descriptors.

evidence.requirement: Preserve existing archive and current records
evidence.summary: Archive A100 retained SHA-256 0de27a1d61bb807648a9b5bb612dbb131549c3aa6018fae839a021270e79d957; current A101 remains the first record.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 remained unchanged; the implementation uses installed Python 3.12.

Healthy pre-restart boot ID 739c9792-2418-47cc-a875-95b27428f3fc was captured, reboot acknowledged, and execution returned with changed boot ID 88ca5d21-0db7-4d16-860e-2376509a81ed. System state, SSH, chronyd, SELinux, code, and data recovered.
System is running with no failed units, expected listeners only, SELinux Enforcing, no test artifacts, no writer process, and no open target descriptors.
